key_insight: WFDroneBench shows that combining risk-aware sensor placement with optimized drone routing can substantially speed up wildfire detection, especially when the risk map is accurate.
engineering_relevance: The benchmark provides a reproducible way to test how well wildfire monitoring systems trade off prediction quality, infrastructure placement, and drone dispatch under realistic scenarios.
method: Open-source Python benchmark integrating learned wildfire risk maps with optimization-based deployment.
Evaluates sensor placement, charging-station placement, and drone routing using standardized wildfire simulations.
Compares two ground-detector and three drone-routing strategies across many scenarios.
evidence_signal: The benchmark covers 7,746 scenarios across 49 locations and the experiments show Max-Coverage achieves the fastest detection on the hardest fires when risk maps are sufficiently accurate.
watch_item: Performance depends strongly on risk-map quality, so a weak or biased map can reduce the benefit of risk-aware deployment.
paper_title: WFDroneBench: A Benchmark for Sensor Placement and Drone Routing for Wildfire Detection
